intro_en: Group the 16 moons by the planet they orbit. No timer, no score.

groups.fact_en: Ganymede, Jupiter's largest moon, is bigger than the planet Mercury.
groups.hint_en: The four moons Galileo saw in 1610.

groups.fact_en: Enceladus sprays plumes of water ice and vapor from cracks near its south pole.
groups.hint_en: The Cassini spacecraft studied them up close.

groups.fact_en: Titania and Oberon, the two largest, were both discovered by William Herschel in 1787.
Nereid takes about 360 days to go once around Neptune, almost an Earth year.
groups.hint_en: Their planet is the farthest from the Sun.

intro_en: Planets, dwarf planets and the spacecraft that visited them. No timer, no score.

groups.name_en: Planets with two moons or fewer
groups.fact_en: On Mercury, one day from sunrise to sunrise lasts about 176 Earth days, twice its 88-day year.
groups.hint_en: The rocky planets closest to the Sun.

groups.fact_en: Saturn's average density is 687 kg per cubic meter, lower than water's.
groups.hint_en: All four giants have a ring system.

groups.fact_en: Ceres is the only dwarf planet in the inner solar system.
groups.hint_en: One of them was called a planet until 2006.

groups.fact_en: Each one visited a world on this board: Juno reached Jupiter's orbit in 2016, Cassini orbited Saturn, New Horizons flew past Pluto and Dawn orbited Ceres.
groups.hint_en: Look for the explorers, not the places.
